claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is governed by nanoscale chemically ordered clusters in a largely disordered matrix.
Nanoscale ordered clusters strengthen local magnetic exchange interactions.
Nanoscale ordered clusters lower the energy barrier for a magnetostructural transition.
Strengthened magnetic exchange and a lower transition barrier yield high magnetic entropy change with minimal hysteresis.
A well-distributed cluster nanostructure creates effective thermal-conduction pathways.
A well-distributed cluster nanostructure dilutes local strain and thereby preserves mechanical stability.
The proposed initial Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-Si-type alloy is a single-phase, chemically disordered solid solution in its as-cast state.
Annealing at 700–900 °C for 1–24 hours can induce adjustable nanoscale chemical ordering.
The proposed annealing treatment induces ordering without altering the alloy's overall composition.
Annealing-induced ordered regions influence the magnetostructural transition through enhanced localized magnetic interactions and a reduced effective transition barrier.
The annealing-induced ordering increases magnetic entropy change under applied fields below 2 T.
Annealing-induced ordering reduces latent heat and consequently reduces hysteresis.
Ordered clusters interspersed in a disordered matrix provide efficient thermal pathways that accelerate heat exchange.
Ordered clusters distribute internal stresses and maintain mechanical integrity.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimized annealed samples will exhibit increased low-field magnetic entropy change.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimized annealed samples will exhibit reduced thermal hysteresis.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimized annealed samples will exhibit higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimized annealed samples will maintain or improve mechanical strength.
The proposed relationships apply to similar rare-earth-free Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-Si high-entropy alloys annealed at 700–900 °C for 1–24 hours and evaluated near room temperature below 2 T.
The optimal degree and length scale of ordering depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
